rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has Ṭuwā with ḍamma, shortened and without tanwīn; it is treated as an irregular form of ṭāw and a diptote as a place-name.
rows.anchor: وقرئت: طُوَى بالضم والقصر مع عدم التنوين. فتكون معدولاً بها عن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading has Ṭiwā with kasra, shortened and with tanwīn, as a verbal noun meaning repetition; the valley was blessed and sanctified twice.
rows.anchor: بالكسر والقصر والتنوين. مصدراً بوزن الثنى وبمعناه

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub takes Ṭuwā to mean an hour of the night: the valley was sanctified at night, when Moses was called, receiving renewed sanctification.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب: طوى من الليل. أي ساعة. والمعنى قدس لك الوادي

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib lists Ṭuwā as the name of the sacred valley.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكره (الراغب) في المفردات. وأقرب منه، والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bint al-Shati considers it likelier that Ṭuwā is a circumstantial description of the sacred valley, where the distance between earth and heaven was folded away.
rows.anchor: وأقرب منه، والله أعلم، أن تكون حالاً للوادي المقدس، حيث طويت الأبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭughyān means exceeding a limit; in Arabic it can describe water overstepping its bounds to become dangerous.
rows.anchor: الطغيان: تجاوز الحد، ويستعمل لغة في الماء يتجاوز الحد إلى الخطر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses ṭughyān of water as well as human transgression; al-Ḥāqqa 69:11 says the water exceeded its bounds.
rows.anchor: ومنه في القرآن: آية الحاقة 11: {إنا لما طغى الماء حملناكم في الجارية}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭāghiya is also glossed as the flood that destroyed Thamūd.
rows.anchor: وفسروا الطاغية كذلك بالطوفان في قوله تعالى: {فأما ثمود فأهلكوا بالطاغية}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most Qur'anic uses mean exceeding limits through disobedience and disbelief, as in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: على أن أكثر استعماله القرآني، في تجاوز الحد في العصيان والكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word also describes exceeding limits through tyranny, arrogance, and oppression.
rows.anchor: كما جاء بمعنى تجاوز الحد، في التجبر والعتو والظلم، في آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same command explains Moses' mission to Pharaoh in Ṭā Hā 20:24, where God says Pharaoh had transgressed.
rows.anchor: وأسند الطغيان إلى فرعون موسى، في آيتي طه خطاباً لموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invitation echoes the command to Moses and Aaron in Ṭā Hā, including the instruction to speak gently and the hope that Pharaoh might remember or fear.
rows.anchor: فقولا له قولاً ليناً لعله يتذكر أو يخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative is an offer framed with tact and gentleness, as made explicit by the parallel instruction in Ṭā Hā.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام هنا للعرض مع تلطف. وهذا التلطف في عرض الرسالة، صريح في آية طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakā means growth in goodness and blessing; self-purification cleanses the soul and allows its virtues to grow.
rows.anchor: والزكاة النمو عن خير وبركة. وتزكية النفس: أن تتطهر وتنمو فضائلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance is direction to the straight path; the root is associated with a raised rock in water that prevents stumbling and with daylight that makes the path clear.
rows.anchor: والهداية: الإرشاد إلى الطريق المستقيم، ولعل أصل استعماله في الهدى: الصخرة الناتئة في الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God “your Lord” to a Pharaoh who denied Moses' Lord is intended to establish the claim and prepare for “then you will fear”: such fear requires faith in his Lord.
rows.anchor: واللافت هنا إضافة رب إلى كاف الخطاب، مع أن فرعون لم يكن يؤمن برب موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An āya is a sign, often used religiously for proof of God's existence, greatness, unity, power, or the miracles supporting chosen messengers; here it proves Moses was sent by God.
rows.anchor: الآية: العلامة، ويكثر استعمالها - دينياً - في الدلالة على وجود الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the sign “great” magnifies the force of its proof and its support for Moses' mission; to identify it, Bint al-Shati turns to Moses' call in Ṭā Hā.
rows.anchor: ووصفت الآية بالكبرى تعظيماً وتقريراً لقوة دلالتها وبلوغها في تأييد رسالة موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athar is a lasting sign or trace; to leave an effect is to leave a durable trace, and āthār are remains from earlier people.
rows.anchor: من علامة باقية. وأثر فيه تأثيراً، ترك فيه أثراً يبقى، والآثار ما بقي من الماضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īthār means preference, as in Joseph 12:91, al-Aʿlā 87:16, and Ṭā Hā 20:72.
rows.anchor: والإيثار: التفضيل، وبهذا المعنى جاء في آيات:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Ḥashr 59:9, īthār is preferring others over oneself, an expression of generosity and virtue.
rows.anchor: وجاء نقيضاً للأثرة في آية الحشر 9:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īthār can imply choosing what one judges best and most lasting, while athara can imply keeping the chosen things for oneself.
rows.anchor: ويجيء الإيثار بمعنى الإختبار، ملحوظاً فيه أن المرء يختار ما يحسبه أفضل وأبقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʾwā is a place one seeks for refuge, protection, and residence.
rows.anchor: والمأوى: المكان يؤوى إليه ويلاذ ويسكن فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses maʾwā only for the afterlife, with Paradise or with Hell and its other names; this presents the afterlife as the permanent abode and final destination.
rows.anchor: وهو صنيع يشهد بأن القرآن الكريم يقرر أن الدار الآخرة هي المأوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb awā occurs fourteen times in the Qur'an and consistently conveys safety, protection, or refuge, as in the examples cited.
rows.anchor: فيأتي في القرآن أربع عشرة مرة، لا يخطئ الحس فيها جميعاً، معنى المأمن والحمى والملاذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that the verse concerned al-Walīd or Abū Jahl do not restrict its general wording without contextual evidence; occasions of revelation are clues to the circumstances of revelation.
rows.anchor: وكونها نزلت في الوليد أو أبي جهل لا يقتضي الاعتبار بخصوص السبب، حيث لا قرينة تصرف إليه عموم لفظ الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the muṣḥaf writes N as one letter, Bint al-Shati sets aside al-Ṭabarī's views that it means a fish, a tablet of light, or an inkwell: those nouns would be written with three letters.
rows.anchor: يجعلنا نستبعد ابتداء ما نقل الإمام الطبري من اختلاف أهل التأويل فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: A report identifies N with the fish beneath the seventh earth that bears the earths; it was created before heaven and earth, and the earth's movement was steadied by mountains.
rows.anchor: عن "ابن عباس ومجاهد" في هذا الحوت الذي عليه الأرضون، تحت الأرض السابعة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī admits uncertainty about whether “inkwell” is a linguistic or revealed term, a common noun or a proper name, and whether it is diptote.
rows.anchor: وقد صرح الزمخشري بأنه لا يدري - ولا أدري معه - "أهو وضع لغوي أم شرعي؟

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another view makes N the name of the sura; Bint al-Shati finds this unhelpful because the sura would simply be named after its opening letter, as Ṣād and Qāf are.
rows.anchor: وفي قول آخر إن (ن) اسم للسورة. وليس فذ هذا القول ما يغني

rows.speaker: الراغب الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib reads N as the familiar letter of the Arabic alphabet, the interpretation Bint al-Shati finds reassuring.
rows.anchor: ويبدو أن الراغب الأصفهاني، اختار أن تكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qalam is the first sura to open with a disjoined letter; Bint al-Shati says 28 more followed, 26 Meccan and three from the early Medinan period.
rows.anchor: من هذه الحروف المقطعة بفواتح السور، وبعدها نزلت ثمان وعشرون سورة مفتتحة بهذه الحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disjoined letters comprise fourteen distinct letters, half the letters of the Arabic alphabet.
rows.anchor: ومجموع حروفها بغير المكرر منها أربعة حرفاً، هي نصف حروف معجمنا.

rows.speaker: أصحاب هذا القول
rows.claim: One view treats the letters as signs for divine names or attributes, but its adherents do not agree on expansions: N may stand for Helper or Light, for example.
rows.anchor: وأصحاب هذا القول لا يكادون يجمعون على دلالات الحروف فيه،

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: A view calls the letters marks made by the revelation scribes; Bint al-Shati objects that human marks would then occur inside Qur'anic verses after the basmala.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي علامات وضعها كتاب الوحي. ويمنعه أن تدخل هذه العلامات، وهي من قول البشر

rows.speaker: حيى بن أخطب
rows.claim: The abjad theory is identified as an Isrāʾīliyyāt report: Huyayy calculates the letters in alif-lām-mīm as 71 years, then alif-lām-mīm-ṣād as 161 and alif-lām-rāʾ as 271, and questions whether to follow a prophet with that term; the Prophet replies with further letters, leaving the Jews unsure of the term.
rows.anchor: وهذا من إسرائيليات "حيى بن أخطب اليهودي" فتقول الراوية إن أخاه أبا ياسر مر في رجال من يهود

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: Another view makes the letters alerts to what follows, often a mention of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وأكثر ما يكون بعدها ذكر القرآن الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī and Ibn al-Qayyim elaborate the view that the opening letters alert readers to what follows, and Ibn Kathīr surveys its occurrences.
rows.anchor: في (التبيان) واستوفاه "ابن كثير" في تفسيره

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: The letters are among the ambiguous matters whose knowledge God reserves; al-Shaʿbī says every book has a secret and the Qur'an's secret is its opening letters.
rows.anchor: ما روى عن الشعبي أنه سئل عن فواتح السور: إن لكل كتاب سراً وإن سر هذا القرآن فواتح السور.

rows.speaker: ابن القيم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim says the letters honor the alphabet as the building blocks of God's speech and revealed books, and as a gift that enables people to speak.
rows.anchor: واختار ابن القيم أن يكون في افتتاح السور بها، تنبيه على شرف الحروف وعظم قدرها وجلالتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bint al-Shati finds a still closer explanation in the letters showing that the Qur'an is made from the same letters familiar to its Arabic audience, exposing their inability to produce its like.
rows.anchor: وأقرب منه قول من قالوا إن هذه الحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this early Meccan sura, N draws attention to the mystery of the letter in the Qur'an's inimitable eloquence.
rows.anchor: ومجيء الحرف (ن) في (سورة القلم) المكية المبكرة، فيه لفت واضح إلى سر الحرف في البيان المعجز.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the sura answers pagans who deny the Prophet and call the Qur'an old legends, its opening prepares the challenge to produce its like and brings them to confront the proof in their own language and letters.
rows.anchor: فكأن هذه تمهيد للمعاجزة التي تتحداهم أن يأتوا بمثله، واستدراجهم إلى أن تلزمهم الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first revealed word, “Read,” points to God's great sign in creating humans from a clinging form and teaching by the pen; Al-Qalam then opens with N to point to letters as the basis of reading, knowledge, and eloquence.
rows.anchor: وقد كانت كلمة الوحي الأولى "اقرأ" لافته إلى آية الله الكبرى، في الإنسان الذي خلقه سبحانه من علق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An isolated letter supplies no meaning and is nearly only a sound; its greater mystery appears when it takes its place in a word.
rows.anchor: تنطق به منفرداً منقطعاً فلا يعطي أي معنى أو دلالة، بل لا يكاد يخرج عن مجرد صوت

rows.speaker: الإمام الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the oath is by the pen God created and commanded to write everything that will happen until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الطبري إن القلم معروف "غير أن الذي أقسم به ربنا من الأقلام، القلم الذي خلقه تعالى فأمره بكتابه

rows.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim extols the pen as a sign and among God's first creations, by which decree and law were written, revelation and religion recorded, scripture established, knowledge preserved, and human affairs served.
rows.anchor: قال: "فأقسم بالكتاب - ن - وبالقلم الذي هو إحدى آياته وأول مخلوقاته

rows.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim distinguishes twelve ranks of pens, with the pre-eternal pen of divine decree highest and most honored; the oath magnifies it.
rows.anchor: ثم عقد فصلاً في مراتب الأقلام فجعلها اثنى عشر قلماً، أعلاها وأجلها قدراً قلم القدر السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This discussion points toward interpreting the pronoun as the recording angels, who write creatures' fates and deeds in the Preserved Tablet by God's command.
rows.anchor: بأن الضمير في الفعل للحفظة من الملائكة الذين يكتبون بأمر الله أقدار الخلائق وأعمالهم

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another view identifies the pen as the familiar writing implement, honored because God taught by the pen.
rows.anchor: وفيه قول آخر، هو أنه القلم المألوف المعتاد الذي يسطر به الناس كتاباتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bint al-Shati takes the waw as an oath of exaltation, drawing attention to familiar writing and the letter's hidden power as a prelude to answering the pagans' argument.
rows.anchor: الأول في القسم للتعظيم، لملحظ بياني، هو اللفت إلى ما عهدوا من أمر القلم والكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She prefers to take “what they write” as the Arabs who copied ancient legends and tried to liken the Qur'an to them; the verb choice anticipates the accusation in 68:15.
rows.anchor: والأقرب عندنا أن يكون الضمير في {يسطرون} لمن كانوا ينقلون من العرب أساطير القدماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusation that the Qur'an is ancient legends recurs in the cited verses, where disbelievers claim it was copied, recited to the Prophet, or could be matched.
rows.anchor: ونظيره ما في الآيات: {وقالوا أساطير الأولين اكتتبها فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلاً}

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq reports in the Sīra that some Arabs copied ancient legends and recited them to impugn the Prophet; Bint al-Shati invites comparison of those writings with the Qur'an in their language and letters.
rows.anchor: على ما روى "ابن إسحاق" في (السيرة النبوية) . وهذه هي آيات الكتاب المعجز معروضة عليهم بلغتهم وحروفهم

rows.speaker: خديجة
rows.claim: Hadith and sīra accounts depict Muhammad returning from the cave on Laylat al-Qadr distressed; Khadīja reassures him that God will never humiliate him, citing his virtues.
rows.anchor: وأفضى إلى زوجه السيدة خديجة بما رأى وما سمع فقالت رضي الله عنها: أبشر يا ابن العم واثبت

rows.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
rows.claim: Waraqa ibn Nawfal tells Muhammad he is the prophet of this community and will be called a liar, harmed, fought, and expelled.
rows.anchor: "ورقة بن نوفل" لخبر الوحي الأول، وقوله للمصطفى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These assurances fortify the Prophet at the beginning of revelation, prepare him for the burden of conveying the message, and sustain him through the abuse of deniers.
rows.anchor: فندرك عمق أثرها في تثبيت المصطفى وتقوية فؤاده، وتهيئته لما هو بسيل أن يحتمل من أعباء التبليغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes treat “by your Lord's grace” as parenthetical, like saying, “By God's favor, you are virtuous”; Bint al-Shati prefers this simple parsing.
rows.anchor: وجمهرة المفسرين على أن جملة {بنعمة ربك} اعتراضية، كما تقول لصاحبك: أنت بحمد الله فاضل.

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān offers the alternative sense “you are not mad, by your Lord's blessing”; Bint al-Shati rejects it as a meaning-only gloss rather than a syntactic parsing.
rows.anchor: ذكره "أبو حيان" في (البحر) وقال إنه تفسير معنى لا تفسير إعراب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bint al-Shati considers Abū Ḥayyān's construal strained and prefers ordinary Arabic phrasing, like “by God's favor, you are not wretched.”
rows.anchor: وفيه تكلف لا يسيغه حس العربية المرهف الذي يجلوه البيان القرآني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her earlier survey in al-Takāthur found that the Qur'an uses niʿma for worldly blessings and reserves the form naʿīm for the bliss of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقد سبق استقراء ما في القرآن من لفظ نعمة، مادة وصيغة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians treat the bāʾ before majnūn as extra: it governs the word's genitive form while its syntactic position remains nominative, hidden by the preposition's kasra.
rows.anchor: فهي تعمل في لفظ الخبر، ويبقى الحكم الإعرابي على أصله، يمنع من ظهور حركته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across the Qur'an, this bāʾ regularly occurs in the single-word predicate of mā and laysa, with only a few context-specific exceptions.
rows.anchor: وباستقراء ما في القرآن الكريم من خبر ليس وما، يلقانا اطراد وقوع هذه الباء المقول بزيادتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bint al-Shati objects to calling the bāʾ extra, since that would imply it could be removed, a possibility the Qur'anic style does not support.
rows.anchor: ولا يهون القول بأن الباء حرف جر زائد، إذ مقتضى القول بزيادتها إمكان الاستغناء عنها

rows.speaker: النحويون من المفسرين
rows.claim: Grammatical exegetes say the bāʾ is added to intensify the negation; Bint al-Shati instead says it makes the denial categorical.
rows.anchor: والنحويون من المفسرين، يذهبون إلى أن الباء زائدة لتأكيد النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In negative mā or laysa clauses, the bāʾ makes the statement a categorical denial; in interrogative negatives it turns the statement into an insistent affirmation, and the particle consistently remains on the predicate.
rows.anchor: هو أن الباء تأتي في خبر المنفي بما أو ليس، فتجعله جحداً وإنكاراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this verse the bāʾ after mā makes the denial that the Prophet is mad categorical.
rows.anchor: وفي آية القلم، تأتي الباء في خبر المنفي بما، فتصير به إلى إنكار بات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajr originally meant material payment for work or a service; it came to denote moral recompense, for which ajr is used more often than ujra, the usual term in transactions.
rows.anchor: الأجر في أصل الوضع اللغوي، الجزاء المادي على عمل أو منفعة، ومن الإيجاز والاستئجار في المعاملات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In religious terminology, ajr means reward, with attention to what returns from an act.
rows.anchor: ثم جاء الأجر في المصطلح الديني، بمعنى الثواب، ملحوظاً فيه ما يعود من جزاء العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Qur'an, ajr retains its original sense in references to women's bridal payments.
rows.anchor: زمن الاستعمال القرآني للأجر بمعناه الأول، الأجور في مهور النساء:

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's interpretation implies that acts of grace may be subject to reproach, but wages for deeds are not.
rows.anchor: وإنما تمن الفواضل لا الأجور على الأعمال

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī's interpretation as a Muʿtazilite subterfuge.
rows.anchor: أنكره "أبو حيان" ورأى فيه "دسيسة اعتزال".

rows.speaker: ابن المنير الإسكندري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munīr also rejects that reading, citing the Prophet's report that no one enters Paradise by deeds alone, even the Prophet, without God's favor and mercy; he says the reading implies God owes Paradise as a duty.
rows.anchor: وكذلك أنكره "ابن المنير الإسكندري"، فقال في (الانتصاف) :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bint al-Shati says God may favor servants and remind them of blessings; human reproach is blameworthy when arrogant or transactional, so the verse means an uncounted reward unmarred by anything that spoils it, not al-Zamakhsharī's reading.
rows.anchor: فنطمئن إلى تفسيره بأنه أجر غير معدود ولا مشوب بما ينغضه. وليس على الوجه الذي ذهب إليه "الزمخشري".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite form ajr conveys an unrestricted, general reward, not limited by a definite description.
rows.anchor: وتنكير "أجر" يفيد الإطلاق، والتعميم غير المقيد بتعريف يخصصه.

rows.speaker: الإمام الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits ʿĀʾisha's explanation of the Prophet's character: “His character was the Qur'an.”
rows.anchor: نقل "الإمام الطبري" قول من فهموها بحديث السيدة عائشة رضي الله عنها، أنها سئلت عن خلق الرسول

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha answers that the Prophet's character was the Qur'an; Bint al-Shati notes the chronological objection that this is an early Meccan verse, before much of the Qur'an's moral teaching had been revealed.
rows.anchor: أنها سئلت عن خلق الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقالت: كان خلقه القرآن. وقد يرد عليه أن الآية مكية مبكرة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret the phrase as “a great religion,” meaning Islam; Bint al-Shati rejects this because the Qur'an nowhere uses khuluq to mean religion.
rows.anchor: وفسرها بعضهم بالدين: وإنك لعلى دين عظيم، وهو الإسلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse confirms God's knowledge of the Prophet's high character, recognized since boyhood and in his youth for trustworthiness, truthfulness, nobility, and chastity.
rows.anchor: وإنما تؤكد الآية، ما علم الله من خلق نبيه المصطفى،

rows.speaker: أبو طالب
rows.claim: At Muhammad and Khadīja's marriage, Abū Ṭālib praised Muhammad as unmatched among Quraysh youths in honor, nobility, merit, and intellect.
rows.anchor: أو كما قال عمه أبو طالب في خطبة زواج محمد من خديجة بنت خويلد:

rows.speaker: خديجة
rows.claim: Khadīja says God will not humiliate Muhammad because he keeps kinship ties, speaks truth, fulfills trusts, bears burdens, hosts guests, and helps in times of hardship.
rows.anchor: وقالت أم المؤمنين الأولى، رضى الله عنها، في ليلة القدر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports also say Quraysh called Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh “the trustworthy” before his prophetic mission.
rows.anchor: ومعهاما تواتر به الخبر من لقب الأمين الذي أطلقته قريش على محمد بن عبد الله قبل المبعث.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This early revelation is God's testimony to the Prophet's great character, crowning his known virtues and strengthening him against arrogant deniers.
rows.anchor: شهادة إلهية بعظمة خلق المصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام، تتوج ما كان معروفاً من مكارم أخلاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣar originally means sight by the eye, as in the cited Qur'anic examples.
rows.anchor: أصل الاستعمال اللغوي في البصر، للعين الباصرة، ومنه في القرآن الكريم مثل آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense tied to straying is closer to the rhetorical feel and the following verse's contrast between those astray from God's path and the guided.
rows.anchor: الضلال أقرب إلى حس البيان، كما أنه أقرب إلى سياق الآية بعده:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance and straying originally describe finding or losing a road, literally and figuratively; they acquire the Islamic senses of faith and disbelief here, while “path” preserves the original metaphor.
rows.anchor: وأصلهما في الضلال عن الطريق أو الإهتداء إليع، حسياً ومعنوياً. ثم نقلا إلى الدلالة الإسلامية على الكفر والإيمان،

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reads the wording as an indirect allusion: God knows that Muhammad is guided and the Quraysh unbelievers have strayed from truth; Bint al-Shati prefers this to al-Zamakhsharī's alternatives.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري: "وهذا من معاريض الكلام، وإنما معنى الكلام: إن ربك يا محمد هو أعلم بك وأنك المهتدي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī suggests God knows the rational people, who are guided, or that the verse promises and threatens the two groups with their respective recompense; Bint al-Shati prefers al-Ṭabarī's allusive reading.
rows.anchor: وهذا أقرب من قول الزمخشري: "هو أعلم بالعقلاء وهم المهتدون، أو يكون وعيداً ووعداً بجزاء الفريقين".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse leaves unspoken the lesser comparison implied by “more knowing”; Arabic permits this without supplying an omitted “than you” or “than anyone else.”
rows.anchor: والآية أمسكت عن ذكر مفضول * أعلم * وهذا يطلقه من قيد المفاضلة بين عالم وأعلم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers here reject God's signs and the prophethood of His messenger.
rows.anchor: التكذيب هنا، بآيات الله ونبوة رسوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhān means softness, leniency, or accommodation; mudāhana is evasive compromise or disingenuous appeasement.
rows.anchor: والإدهان: اللين والتساهل والمداراة, والمداهنة التحايل واللاينة والمداجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root relates to oil used to soften or smooth: dahān is dye or paint, and dahīn describes a slippery place as if oiled.
rows.anchor: وترجع استعمالات المادة وصيغها في الأصل اللغوي إلى الدهن، يتخذ للتليين والتطرية
